direction: Use internal-geometry-preserving cluster rotations as basin-hopping moves: cluster the 122 core points into 8--12 groups by spherical $k$-means (implemented in NumPy, cosine distance, 20 restarts), pick one cluster of 5--18 points, choose a random two-plane in $\mathbb R^9$ (for example spanned by the cluster centroid and a random orthogonal direction), and rotate only that cluster by $0.15$, $0.3$, or $0.6$ radians, or reflect it across a random hyperplane. direction: Search from algebraically structured seeds unrelated to the record basin: build a candidate pool from normalized nonzero integer vectors in $\{-1,0,1\}^9$ (19,682 vectors; optionally also entries in $\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$ subsampled), including $D_9$-type vectors $(\pm1,\pm1,0^7)/\sqrt2$ and coordinate vectors, then greedily select 131 vectors minimizing the running maximum dot, followed by swap improvement in which one selected point is replaced by one pool vector if it lowers the maximum or reduces the number of near-maximal pairs. idea: Target-lowering feasibility homotopy with annealed softplus all-pairs penalty and analytic L-BFGS gradients from large perturbations, with only sparse LP squeezes.
direction: Replace local max-minimization by a target-lowering feasibility homotopy: set targets $t=0.4223,0.4220,0.4217,0.4213$ in sequence and, for each, minimize the all-pairs smooth penalty $\sum_{i<j}\mathrm{softplus}((\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-t)/\tau)^2$ with $\tau$ annealed from $10^{-3}$ to $10^{-4}$, using analytic gradients and SciPy L-BFGS on unconstrained variables renormalized inside the objective, starting from perturbations of the incumbent with scale $0.05$--$0.15$ rather than $0.01$. Allow temporary violations of the current record during optimization, promote a result only when its penalty is near zero or its true maximum improves, and interleave at most two short tangent-LP calls before the final 20-second LP; this deliberately seeks a configuration feasible below the record instead of asking the already jammed LP optimum for another infinitesimal improvement.

idea: Target-feasibility descent with annealed softplus violation penalty on the core plus exhaustive hole reinsertion for rattlers, accepting only true max-cosine improvements.
direction: Use target-feasibility optimization to force the rattlers to engage: successively set targets $\tau=0.4220,0.4215,0.4210,\ldots$ and minimize a capped violation penalty such as $\sum_{i<j}\mathrm{softplus}((\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-\tau)/T)^2$ with $T$ annealed from $3\times10^{-3}$ to $2\times10^{-4}$, rather than minimizing only the current maximum. At each $\tau$, first remove the nine rattlers, run tangential Adam on the 122 core points under the $\tau$-penalty so that oversized holes can shrink and core contacts can break, then reinsert each rattler by sampling at least 20,000 random sphere points, choosing the point minimizing its maximum core cosine, locally refining it, and jointly re-polishing all 131 points; accept the configuration only if its true maximum is below the previous $\tau$, otherwise decrease the step in $\tau$ and retry from the last feasible point. Reserve only the final 20 seconds for LP polishing, since feasibility pressure—not LP—is the mechanism for creating a new active set.

idea: Multi-point hub surgery deleting 3/5/8 high-degree contacts at once with sequential largest-hole reinsertion, moderate softmax tangential polish, and a graph-dissimilar 3-elite archive with final LP squeeze.
direction: Perform explicit multi-point contact-graph surgery on hubs rather than single-point kicks: compute contact degrees at threshold $10^{-7}$, choose subsets of 3, 5, or 8 points biased toward degrees above 20, delete the whole subset simultaneously, and reinsert its points sequentially into jointly recomputed largest holes found from random sampling plus single-point softmax refinement against all retained and already reinserted points. After each surgery, run a moderate—not fully converged—weighted tangential polish, evaluate the exact maximum and the Jaccard distance between the new and old contact graphs, and maintain an archive of three elites that are mutually graph-dissimilar as well as low-scoring; iterate surgery from different archive members and give the overall best a final LP polish. Requiring simultaneous hub deletion and graph novelty prevents the optimizer from immediately restoring the deleted contacts.

idea: Escape the over-jammed 122-point core by large topology-changing surgery (hub extinction with greedy hole re-insertion, random-cap transplants and fresh basins) followed by annealed soft-max repulsion, reserving trust-region LP only for promising basins.

Build independent lattice/signed-permutation/orbit pools, greedy-select 131 points, swap-optimize max then count>0.40, then smoothed repulsion and short trust-region LP to reach a distinct symmetric basin.
direction: Search from structured algebraic and lattice configurations completely independent of the record: generate normalized candidate pools from integer vectors in $\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}^9$, signed-permutation patterns, the $D_9$, $A_9$, and $E_8\times A_1$ root/lattice shells, and low-parameter group orbits of a few seed vectors under signed coordinate permutations. From each pool, greedily select 131 points minimizing the resulting maximum cosine, improve the selection by repeated one-out/one-in swaps that reduce first the maximum and then the number of pairs above $0.40$, and only then apply fast smoothed repulsion and a short LP polish. Compare several pool constructions within the time budget and retain the best distinct basin; this directly tests whether the missing structure is a symmetric/lattice-like arrangement that perturbations of the record cannot reach.

idea: From-scratch log-sum-exp continuation with projected Adam, geometric beta increase, early pruning and spectral clustering plus tail polish.
direction: Run a from-scratch smooth-continuation search over many independent random basins: for each seed, minimize $\left(\sum_{i<j}\exp(\beta\langle x_i,x_j\rangle)\right)^{1/\beta}$ or an equivalent log-sum-exp objective with $\beta$ increased geometrically from about 20 to 400, using projected Adam with cosine-decayed step size and exact renormalization, so early optimization can reorganize global clusters before late optimization enforces equioscillation. Use numerous shorter runs with different seeds and initial $\beta$ schedules, discard runs rapidly if their smoothed score is uncompetitive after a fixed fraction of the budget, cluster survivors by sorted pair-cosine spectra/contact signatures, and polish only the best representative of each distinct cluster. This explores configurations whose global cluster organization differs from the record instead of spending the entire 180 seconds repeatedly collapsing random perturbations back into that record's basin.

idea: Archive-based basin hopping that forces contact-topology changes via frozen-core subset re-optimization and largest-hole reinsertion of jammed/rattler points, alternated with annealed log-sum-exp Adam repulsion and trust-region LP polishing.

Simultaneous hub-deletion surgery on 3/5/8 high-degree core points with sequential largest-hole reinsertion plus periodic rattler-absorption moves, moderate softmax tangential polish, and a Jaccard-dissimilar 3-elite archive with final LP squeeze.

idea: Dihedral-symmetric orbit search with annealed log-sum-exp Adam on seeds then symmetry release and LP polish to a new basin.
direction: Search a symmetric orbit ansatz, then break the symmetry. Use the dihedral group of coordinate permutations generated by the cyclic shift and reversal of the 9 coordinates (order 18): choose 7 random seed vectors in $\mathbb{R}^9$, generate their 126 orbit points by all 18 signed-permutation-free coordinate permutations ($\texttt{np.roll}$ and reversal), and add 5 free special points to reach 131, removing/replacing any near-duplicates within an orbit (cosine $>0.99$) by perturbing that seed. Optimise only the $7\times9+5\times9$ seed parameters with projected Adam on the full $131\times131$ Gram matrix, log-sum-exp $\alpha$ annealed $30\to300$, learning rate $0.01\to0.001$, for at most 60s and several random restarts, because the symmetry ties coordinates together and prevents the amorphous 800-contact jamming pattern. Take the best symmetric configuration, then release the constraint: add tiny independent noise ($10^{-3}$) to every generated point, run 1500 ordinary repulsion steps and up to 40s of LP polish, evaluating against the loaded record throughout and returning whichever is better. Even if the symmetric ansatz is not itself optimal, its released version lands in a genuinely different basin with a structured, evenly-loaded contact graph.

idea: Relocate overloaded core points into global holes with basin-hopping acceptance to change contact topology instead of re-polishing the same rigid graph.
Grow to 131 from a relaxed 110-point core optimized with annealed LSE-Adam then greedy hole insertion plus hinge soft-repulsion to inherit a different contact topology.
direction: Build up from an optimised smaller code instead of perturbing the full 131-point record. Remove the 9 rattlers and the 3–13 points with the largest per-point maximum cosine/highest degree to obtain starting codes of size $N=109$–$122$, optimise each smaller code hard with annealed log-sum-exp Adam ($\alpha:20\to400$, 3000–6000 vectorised steps, checking elapsed time every 50 steps) until its max cosine drops clearly below 0.42245 (smaller codes have slack, so this should be attainable), then greedily grow back to 131: at each size, generate 20,000 candidate hole points, take the 30 candidates with smallest maximum cosine to the current code, refine each against the current code, insert the best, and run 400 global soft-repulsion steps with a hinge penalty $\sum \max(0,\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-0.42245)^2$ plus weak log-sum-exp so existing good pairs are disturbed as little as possible. If an insertion stalls above 0.43, backtrack that insertion and try the next-best geometrically distinct hole (cosine $<0.9$ to the failed candidate). Reserve the final 30s for LP polish only. This cardinality path reaches 131 through a sequence of feasible, differently-connected configurations, so the final contact graph is inherited from a relaxed core rather than from the jammed record.

idea: Force rattlers to engage with annealed capped-violation targets instead of polishing the max.
direction: Use target-feasibility optimization to force the rattlers to engage: successively set targets $\tau=0.4220,0.4215,0.4210,\ldots$ and minimize a capped violation penalty such as $\sum_{i<j}\mathrm{softplus}((\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-\tau)/T)^2$ with $T$ annealed from $3\times10^{-3}$ to $2\times10^{-4}$, rather than minimizing only the current maximum. At each $\tau$, first remove the nine rattlers, run tangential Adam on the 122 core points under the $\tau$-penalty so that oversized holes can shrink and core contacts can break, then reinsert each rattler by sampling at least 20,000 random sphere points, choosing the point minimizing its maximum core cosine, locally refining it, and jointly re-polishing all 131 points; accept the configuration only if its true maximum is below the previous $\tau$, otherwise decrease the step in $\tau$ and retry from the last feasible point. Reserve only the final 20 seconds for LP polishing, since feasibility pressure—not LP—is the mechanism for creating a new active set.

idea: Escape the over-jammed 122-core by multi-point cap resampling and hub-neighbourhood reshuffling with annealed soft-max repulsion and wandering acceptance instead of single-point kicks plus LP.

Degree-equalized annealed basin-hopping that relieves over-jammed hubs via coordinated multi-point void reinsertion, hub-rattler swaps and cap shakes screened by momentum LSE tangential descent with Metropolis wandering plus final LP squeeze.
Delete rattlers plus random hubs and greedily reinsert into frozen-core holes with large random sampling plus softmax refinement, then Adam LSE and global repulsion with LP squeeze.
direction: Rattler-plus-hub deletion and frozen-core hole reinsertion. Load `best.npy`, compute the contact graph at threshold $10^{-7}$, identify the 9 rattlers and all points of contact degree $\ge 22$. In each trial (until $t=130$s), delete the rattlers plus a random subset of 4–12 hubs, freeze the remaining $\sim$110–118 points, and reinsert the deleted points one at a time: sample 30,000 random sphere candidates, score each by its maximum cosine to the frozen-plus-already-reinserted set, keep the best 20, locally refine each by 100 tangential softmax-repulsion steps ($T=0.01$, step 0.02) against that set, and insert the best refined candidate. Then optimise only the reinserted coordinates (frozen set fixed) for 300 Adam steps on a log-sum-exp objective with $\alpha$ annealed $60\to300$, unfreeze all points for 600–1200 fast weighted-repulsion steps, evaluate the true max cosine, and retain the result only if it beats the incumbent; finish with at most 25s of the trust-region LP and always return the incumbent on timeout. This directly attacks the diagnosed imbalance: it gives hubs room, forces rattlers into genuine holes, and changes which pairs are contacts rather than re-polishing the same graph.

idea: Grow from a relaxed smaller core: prune rattlers plus hubs, anneal the core with log-sum-exp Adam, then greedily reinsert holes with hinge-constrained soft repulsion and LP finish.
direction: Build up from an optimised smaller code instead of perturbing the full 131-point record. Remove the 9 rattlers and the 3–13 points with the largest per-point maximum cosine/highest degree to obtain starting codes of size $N=109$–$122$, optimise each smaller code hard with annealed log-sum-exp Adam ($\alpha:20\to400$, 3000–6000 vectorised steps, checking elapsed time every 50 steps) until its max cosine drops clearly below 0.42245 (smaller codes have slack, so this should be attainable), then greedily grow back to 131: at each size, generate 20,000 candidate hole points, take the 30 candidates with smallest maximum cosine to the current code, refine each against the current code, insert the best, and run 400 global soft-repulsion steps with a hinge penalty $\sum \max(0,\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-0.42245)^2$ plus weak log-sum-exp so existing good pairs are disturbed as little as possible. If an insertion stalls above 0.43, backtrack that insertion and try the next-best geometrically distinct hole (cosine $<0.9$ to the failed candidate). Reserve the final 30s for LP polish only. This cardinality path reaches 131 through a sequence of feasible, differently-connected configurations, so the final contact graph is inherited from a relaxed core rather than from the jammed record.

idea: Rigid half-code rotation surgery preserving intra-part Gram exactly while hill-climbing the cross-block smooth-max over SO(9) antisymmetric generators plus short repulsion settling.
direction: Rigid cluster-rotation surgery that preserves intra-cluster cosines exactly. Partition the incumbent into two halves by the sign of the first principal component (or by spherical $k$-means with $k=2$–$4$ run in numpy), then rotate one part by $R=\exp(\theta A)$, where $A$ is a random antisymmetric $9\times9$ matrix normalised to $\|A\|_F=1$ and $\theta\in[0.05,0.45]$; this leaves all within-part inner products unchanged and alters only cross-part pairs, so a good substructure cannot be destroyed by the move. Optimise the rotation directly over its 36 antisymmetric parameters with derivative-free search: propose Gaussian perturbations of $A$ (scale 0.05–0.2), accept a proposal only if the smooth maximum ($\alpha=200$) of the cross-part Gram block decreases, run 300–800 such proposals per surgery (each is just a $65\times66$ Gram computation), and try several partitions/angles until $t=120$s. After each accepted rotation, run only 300–800 fast repulsion steps to let the interface settle, accept the configuration globally only if the true max cosine improves, and otherwise revert to the incumbent before the next surgery; cap the final LP polish at 30s with a hard internal deadline of 170s. Coordinated rigid motion of $\sim$65 points changes hundreds of cross contacts simultaneously—exactly the collective move that single-point kicks and the tangent LP cannot make.

idea: Load-balanced basin hopping that relieves the over-jammed core by transplanting high-contact hubs into deepest holes plus uniform background repulsion to activate rattlers, with annealing acceptance and LP squeeze.
